rows.source: HSE sharps and needlestick injury prevention
rows.verified: Blood-contaminated sharps can transmit bloodborne viruses through percutaneous injury.

rows.source: HSE sharps and needlestick injury prevention
rows.verified: Where sharps are necessary, employers should consider whether a safer sharps device can be used.

rows.source: HSE sharps and needlestick injury prevention
rows.verified: Work involving sharps must be risk assessed to identify how injuries could occur.

rows.source: HSE sharps and needlestick injury prevention
rows.verified: Needles and other sharps should not be bent or forced during handling.

rows.source: HSE sharps and needlestick injury prevention
rows.verified: Suitable personal protective equipment may supplement, but not replace, safer handling controls.

rows.source: HSE sharps and needlestick injury prevention
rows.verified: Used sharps should be disposed of immediately in an appropriate sharps container.

rows.source: HSE sharps and needlestick injury prevention
rows.verified: Needles should not be reused, resheathed or recapped unless an essential exception is risk assessed and controlled.

rows.source: HSE sharps and needlestick injury prevention
rows.verified: Workers should be trained in safe use, disposal and the response required after a sharps injury.

rows.source: HSE sharps and needlestick injury prevention
rows.verified: Sharps risk depends on device, procedure, contamination, handling, disposal, worker competence, protective controls and response time.

rows.source: HSE sharps and needlestick injury prevention
rows.verified: HSE sharps evidence is device-, procedure-, patient-, worker-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.

rows.source: HSE violence and aggression at work controls
rows.verified: Health and safety law requires employers to protect workers from work-related violence and aggression.

rows.source: HSE violence and aggression at work controls
rows.verified: HSE's definition includes abuse, threats and assaults connected with work activity.

rows.source: HSE violence and aggression at work controls
rows.verified: Employers must assess significant violence risks and implement effective control measures.

rows.source: HSE violence and aggression at work controls
rows.verified: Workers and their representatives should be consulted when violence risks are assessed and controlled.

rows.source: HSE violence and aggression at work controls
rows.verified: Control measures should address workplace design, work organisation, communication and security where relevant.

rows.source: HSE violence and aggression at work controls
rows.verified: Training can include recognition of warning signs, communication skills and incident procedures.

rows.source: HSE violence and aggression at work controls
rows.verified: De-escalation and emergency arrangements should be proportionate to the assessed risk.

rows.source: HSE violence and aggression at work controls
rows.verified: Employers should support affected workers, record and report qualifying incidents, and review controls after events.

rows.source: HSE violence and aggression at work controls
rows.verified: Workplace-violence risk depends on sector, task, public contact, lone working, environment, staffing, controls and local incident patterns.

rows.source: HSE violence and aggression at work controls
rows.verified: HSE violence evidence is workplace-, task-, worker-, offender-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level assault probability.
